content: The COVID-19 pandemic has had a profound impact on the mental health of individuals with diabetes. People living with diabetes have reported experiencing heightened levels of psychological distress, which can be attributed to factors such as prolonged isolation, anxiety about the risk of infection, and limitations on social interactions. These mental health challenges are particularly severe among elderly individuals with diabetes, who are also more likely to struggle with feelings of loneliness. There has been a noticeable increase in the prevalence of depression, anxiety, and stress-related symptoms within this population. These issues are largely driven by the ongoing restrictions imposed during the pandemic, a reduction in physical activity, and disruptions to regular dietary habits. Many individuals with diabetes have encountered significant obstacles in maintaining a consistent and healthy lifestyle, which has further complicated their ability to effectively manage their condition. This, in turn, has negatively affected their overall quality of life.
